name: Property-Based Residence

requirements.blocker_text: A non-EU/OECD foreigner who purchases residential property valued at least EUR 40,000 may obtain temporary residence status on that basis, renewable, typically for around 1 year at a time.
requirements.fix_path: Purchase qualifying residential property worth at least EUR 40,000 and apply for temporary residence.

requirements.blocker_text: Invest North Macedonia's own guidance separately lists EU/OECD nationals who own property in the country as a category with special eligibility for temporary residence -- without stating a minimum property value for this group, in contrast to the specific EUR 40,000 threshold stated for non-EU/OECD nationals.
requirements.fix_path: As an EU/OECD national, own qualifying residential property in North Macedonia and apply for temporary residence on that basis.

evidence_required.document: Proof of funds for the purchase

sources.title: Lawyers Antevski (law firm) -- kinds of residence permits in North Macedonia, including the EUR 40,000 non-EU/OECD property-purchase threshold and the 5-year continuous-temporary-residence rule for permanent residence
Invest North Macedonia (government investment-promotion agency) -- special temporary-residence eligibility for EU/OECD nationals who own property in North Macedonia

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (North Macedonia). STATUS: DRAFT -- the quantified EUR 40,000 threshold for non-EU/OECD nationals is sourced only to a law firm (tier 3); a government-hosted statement of this specific figure was not located, so the file stays draft even though a government source (tier 1, Invest North Macedonia) does independently confirm that property-owning EU/OECD nationals have a parallel eligibility path. GENUINE, DISCLOSED ASYMMETRY: the two sources describe two different eligibility structures for two different nationality groups (a stated EUR 40,000 minimum for non-EU/OECD nationals; an unquantified 'ownership' standard for EU/OECD nationals) -- this is disclosed as a real asymmetry in the sourcing, not smoothed into one uniform threshold. This is a passive real-estate-based route, not an active-investment/business-equity route -- modeled under 'business' as the closest available category bucket, consistent with how this dataset has modeled other countries' passive-income/property residence routes. work_rights set 'none' since property-based residence is not described as employment-authorizing.
